applicableAreas: All electric easement areas and proposed structures within 15 feet of easement boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts all buildings and easements but contains NO dimension callouts showing clearances from building structures to electric easement boundaries. Dimension callouts present only measure from buildings to overall property lines (e.g., Bldg 4 is 27.3' from east property line) rather than to the interior boundaries of adjacent electric easements. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) similarly shows easement boundaries but provides no dimensioned verification of clearances from structures. Facts.md documents that two critical easements (Greenbelt Access & Use Easement covering 0.31 acres in NE interior, and City of Austin Drainage Easement covering 0.130 acres in NE corner) are NOT depicted on the site plan, creating further ambiguity about clearance compliance. Multiple electric easements are shown (5' Electric Easements on east/south perimeter, 5' P.U.E., etc.) but no clearance verification exhibits with specific measurements demonstrating compliance with 15-foot clearance requirements for overhead facilities are provided.
findings.reasoning: The grouping requires clearance verification exhibits showing existing electric easements with dimensions from easement boundaries to proposed structures. The site plan adequately shows the location of buildings and easements, but affirmatively demonstrates NO clearance dimensions. While the site plan is otherwise complete, the absence of specific clearance callouts makes compliance verification impossible—the burden is on the applicant to affirmatively demonstrate clearance compliance, not on the reviewer to measure unmarked plans. This deficiency applies to all structures within 15 feet (for overhead facilities) of electric easement boundaries. Facts.md further documents that two major easements affecting the northeast corner are not depicted on submitted plans, which directly impacts the ability to verify clearances related to those undepicted easements.
findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not show existing electric easements with dimension callouts demonstrating clearances from easement boundaries to proposed structures. Provide dimensioned clearance details for all structures located within 15 feet of electric easement boundaries, showing that horizontal sky-to-ground clearance of 7.5 feet and 15-foot radius clearance from overhead conductors are maintained per UCM § 1.10.3.

applicableAreas: All electric easement labels shown on Sheets 2, 9, 11, and 21
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) reveals electric easements labeled as: 'Elec. Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' Sheet 2 (Plat) shows easements labeled '3' Elec. Ease.' and 'Exist 5' Elec. Ease.' Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows '5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883 O.P.R.T.C.Tx.' Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) similarly shows '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 / Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 885 D.R.T.C.Tx.' All instances use abbreviated terminology: 'Elec.' for Electric, 'Tele.' for Telephone, 'P.U.E.' for Public Utility Easement, and 'Ease.' for Easement. The full proper nomenclature 'Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement' is not used on any sheet.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 (Application Requirements for Austin Energy Land Development Review) requires that easements serving electric facilities be clearly and properly labeled. The grouping specifically identifies that abbreviated forms (ETE, EE, Elec. Easement) are non-compliant and must be replaced with complete proper nomenclature. The plans consistently use abbreviated terminology across four sheets, indicating a systematic nomenclature deficiency rather than isolated labeling error. The abbreviations fail to convey the complete scope and type of utilities accommodated within the easements (distribution, telecommunications, fiber).
findings.comment: All electric easement labels use abbreviated forms ('Elec.', 'Tele.', 'Ease.') rather than complete proper nomenclature. Update all easement labels on site plan, plat, grading plan, and electrical design plan to read 'Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement' with the appropriate width designation (e.g., '5' Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement').

applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities and associated easements on north, east, south, and west perimeter of site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) vision analysis identified that overhead electric facilities are present on the perimeter, denoted by dashed lines with '-OHE-' notation (standard symbology for Overhead Electric). However, these same facilities are labeled with generic 'Elec. Easement' terminology without the 'aerial' designation. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) similarly does not distinguish between overhead and underground facilities in its easement labels. The electrical design plan shows 'Underground Electric Line' labels for proposed subsurface facilities within the development, but existing overhead facilities on the perimeter are not designated as 'Aerial electric easement.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.24 requires Austin Energy to obtain easements adequate for safe construction, operation, maintenance, and access. The regulatory overview in the grouping emphasizes that 'Plans must explicitly designate easements as aerial when overhead facilities are present—generic electric easement labels are insufficient.' The presence of overhead facilities (-OHE- notation) is confirmed on the plans, but the associated easements are not labeled to denote their aerial nature. This creates ambiguity regarding the clearance and access requirements applicable to the easement, as aerial and underground easements have distinct dimensional and operational requirements. The absence of 'aerial' designation obscures whether the easement width and clearance provisions accommodate overhead conductors and pole structures.
findings.comment: Overhead electric facilities are present on the site but are not designated with 'aerial electric easement' label; generic electric easement label used instead. Revise all easement labels for facilities showing overhead lines (marked -OHE-) to explicitly read 'Aerial electric distribution easement' on all affected sheets, with appropriate width designation.

applicableAreas: Electric easements on east and south property boundaries; all electric facilities requiring 24/7 access
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a continuous concrete retaining wall running the entire north, east, and south perimeter of the property, physically separating the interior townhome complex from the exterior easement areas. Vision analysis confirms: 'Easements running along the East and South boundaries appear entirely cut off from the public right-of-way (Valley View Road located on far west)... Accessing them from the street requires navigating through private internal drives, bypassing the townhome structures, and traversing the continuous Concrete Retaining Wall.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows NO explicitly labeled access routes (e.g., 'Electric Access Route' or 'Maintenance Path') designated exclusively for electric facilities. While transformer pads on the west side of the property are adjacent to the main driveway loop and are accessible, the 'Electric Easement' areas on the east and south perimeters, as well as pull boxes and other underground facilities in those areas, have no demonstrated access from public ROW. The plan notes 'No explicitly labeled maintenance paths or access routes designated for servicing the electric, telecom, or greenbelt utility easements.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 (Access to AE Facilities) and UCM § 1.14.4 (Access—Transmission Facilities) require that Austin Energy maintain permanent, unobstructed 24/7 vehicular access to all electric facilities for installation, operation, and maintenance. The defining requirement is that access must be available from public right-of-way without traversing private property or encountering physical obstructions. The site plan affirmatively demonstrates that easement areas on the east and south are separated from public street access by a continuous retaining wall; access to these areas requires routing through private internal driveway systems and bypassing residential buildings. This configuration fails to provide the 'unobstructed' access required by code. Further, the plan contains no explicit access route designations for electric maintenance, leaving access provisions ambiguous. The grouping's common violation pattern identifies this exact deficiency: 'Access shown but not dimensioned' or 'no access route from public ROW is shown.'
findings.comment: 24/7 vehicular access to electric easements and facilities on east and south boundaries is not provided from public right-of-way; access is obstructed by continuous concrete retaining wall and requires routing through private internal drives. Show explicit 24/7 maintenance access routes for all electric easements and facilities, with all-weather surface extending from public right-of-way, and dimension all clearances and route widths. Demonstrate that access does not require traversing private property or passing through gates/fencing without 24-hour key/lock provision.

applicableAreas: All electric easement areas shown on grading plan
findings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) delineates easement boundaries (5' Electric Easements, 5' P.U.E., 25' Drainage Easement, etc.) but provides NO explicit surface material specifications (HMAC pavement, PCC concrete, gravel, grass, or unpaved) within the electric easement areas. Vision analysis of Sheet 11 confirms: 'There are very few explicit surface material specifications written directly within the easement areas...surfaces are largely indicated by functional line work and symbols rather than distinct material hatching...general grass, gravel, or asphalt specifications are not explicitly labeled within the utility or drainage easements.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) notes that transformer pads are 'located in spaces containing overlapping circular symbols indicating tree canopies, suggesting these facilities sit in unpaved, landscaped, or natural surface areas, though the exact surface material is not named.' The grading plan legend does not include symbols for surface finish types (grass hatch, gravel hatch, asphalt hatch) that would enable identification of easement surface treatment. The plan shows contours and drainage features within easements but not surface material specifications.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires that drivable surfaces within electric easements be suitable for maintenance vehicles and large bucket trucks. LDC § 25-12-173 Section 202.1 defines 'all-weather driving surface' as Hot Mix Asphaltic Concrete (HMAC) or Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) pavement capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight. Grass, gravel, and unpaved surfaces do not qualify. The grading plan is the appropriate sheet to specify these surface materials, but it lacks explicit callouts. While driveways and parking areas shown in the western portion of the site are clearly delineated as paved (implied by curb lines and pavement specifications in construction details), the eastern and southern electric easement areas are not similarly labeled. The absence of explicit surface specification prevents verification of compliance. This creates genuine ambiguity—the surfaces may be paved (meeting code) or unpaved (failing code), but cannot be determined from the submitted plans.
findings.comment: Drivable surfaces within electric easements are not labeled or specified. Provide explicit surface material specifications (HMAC or PCC pavement) for all electric easement areas on the grading plan and construction details, demonstrating that surfaces are capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight and 32,530 lbs rear axle weight. If any electric easement areas are not paved all-weather surfaces, revise grading/landscaping to provide such surfaces or provide written approval from Austin Energy for alternative surface treatment.

applicableAreas: Electric easement areas on east, south, and northeast portions of property; areas with overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts numerous existing trees (shown as scalloped and dashed circles) overlapping electric easement boundaries. Vision analysis confirms: 'Numerous existing tree symbols (scalloped and dashed circles) are mapped directly overlapping the eastern Greenbelt Access & Use Easement, 15' Easement, and 5' Electric Easement...Tree symbols also heavily overlap the 25' Drainage Easement in the NE corner and the 5' Elec. Easement on the south perimeter.' Additionally, the vision analysis identifies: 'A heavy Concrete Retaining Wall runs continuously inside the North, East, and South perimeters, acting as a physical barrier... A Wood Fence is labeled running along the far East property line...A Pond Perimeter Fence circles the NE corner pond.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) notes transformer pads are 'located in spaces...suggesting these facilities sit in unpaved, landscaped, or natural surface areas.' The site plan shows the retaining wall running through/along the boundary of the Greenbelt Access & Use Easement, and a detention pond with associated fencing directly occupies the 25' Drainage Easement area. No clearance dimensions or tree removal callouts are shown demonstrating that ground-to-sky clearance is maintained.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 7.5 feet minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead conductors within electric easements, and a 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Trees within electric easements create permanent obstructions that violate these clearances and restrict Austin Energy's ability to access and maintain overhead and underground facilities. The presence of trees shown directly overlapping easements, combined with the absence of any tree removal or clearing callouts, demonstrates non-compliance. Further, the concrete retaining wall and associated fence structures running through easement boundaries create physical obstructions that prevent equipment access and violate the ground-to-sky clearance requirement. The grouping's common violation pattern explicitly lists this deficiency: 'Site plan shows building overhang, awning, canopy, or permanent structure extending into or over electric easement, violating ground-to-sky clearance requirement.' Here, trees, walls, and fencing occupy that space.
findings.comment: Ground-to-sky clearances within electric easements are not maintained; existing trees, retaining walls, fencing, and other permanent site improvements are shown directly overlapping easement boundaries. Remove all trees within electric easement boundaries or shown within 15 feet of overhead conductors. Relocate concrete retaining walls and pond perimeter fencing outside easement boundaries or provide written approval from Austin Energy for placement within easements. Provide tree removal and landscape modification details demonstrating 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius clearance from overhead conductors per UCM § 1.10.3.

applicableAreas: Public Utility Easements on north, east, and northeast property; specifically 25' Drainage Easement area and Greenbelt Access & Use Easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows Building 4 positioned 27.3' from the east property line, placing it immediately adjacent to the Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (which occupies NE interior per facts.md). The site plan shows a continuous Concrete Retaining Wall running along the eastern boundary directly adjacent to/through the Greenbelt easement boundary. Vision analysis confirms: 'An Infiltration/Detention Pond and Concrete Retaining Wall sit directly inside the 25' Drainage Easement in the northeast corner...A Concrete Retaining Wall encircles it and Pond Perimeter Fence.' The detention pond structure, retaining walls, and pond fencing represent permanent site improvements placed directly within the 25' Drainage Easement area. Facts.md documents that two critical easements are NOT depicted on the submitted site plan: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (0.31 acres, NE interior—a perpetual no-build zone per recorded Instrument 2010070731); and (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (0.130 acres, NE corner—per recorded Instrument 2011021137). Despite being recorded and binding on the property, these easements were not shown on site plan submittal, yet building placement and pond placement proceed as if these easements do not constrain the layout.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 and UCM § 1.5.2.1.L require that Public Utility Easements serving electric facilities be kept clear of buildings, structures, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, and other permanent improvements without written approval from Austin Energy. The site plan affirmatively shows permanent structures (detention pond with retaining walls and fencing) placed within the 25' Drainage Easement area in the NE corner. These improvements have not been annotated with notation of AE written approval. The Greenbelt easement situation is even more problematic: it is a perpetual no-build zone per the recorded instrument, yet it was not depicted on the site plan, indicating the applicant either did not account for it in the design or deliberately omitted it. Facts.md explicitly states these easements 'must be depicted before approval' and that 'proposed building layout must be evaluated against both easement footprints.' The combined two easements encumber approximately 0.44 acres (~19% of the 2.16-acre site), yet neither is shown on the submitted plans. This constitutes a fundamental deficiency in PUE documentation and compliance.
findings.reasoning_extended: The requirements of UCM § 1.5.2.1.L are explicit: improvements within easements 'May be installed only with written approval from Austin Energy.' The plans show no such approval notation. The regulatory overview states: 'Improvements in PUE without approval' is a common violation pattern. Additionally, the absence of the two critical easements from the site plan—despite their recording and perpetual status—indicates either incomplete survey or intentional omission. Either scenario represents a planning deficiency requiring correction before approval.
findings.comment: Public Utility Easements are not kept clear of site improvements; detention pond with retaining walls and fencing are shown directly within the 25' Drainage Easement in the NE corner. Additionally, critical recorded easements (Greenbelt Access & Use Easement and City of Austin Drainage Easement per facts.md) are not depicted on site plan despite being perpetual encumbrances. Revise site plan to: (1) Depict and label all recorded easements including Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731) and City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137); (2) Remove detention pond, retaining walls, and fencing from within easement boundaries or provide written approval from Austin Energy and City of Austin Watershed Protection; (3) Relocate Building 4 or other structures outside easement buffers; (4) Provide notation on all sheets that improvements have received written AE/City approval if any structures remain within easements.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations shown on electrical design plan and site plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) identifies four transformer pads located at: (1) west side of Bldg. 1; (2) west side of Bldg. 2; (3) east side of Bldg. 4; (4) east side of Bldg. 6 (between Bldg 6 & 7). Vision analysis of Sheet 21 notes: 'Transformer Pad (Typ.) is explicitly labeled on the west side of the property near Bldg 1 and Bldg 2...located immediately adjacent to the main western driveway entrance loop...highly accessible from the vehicular parking areas.' However, the transformer pads on the east side (near Bldgs 4 and 6) are shown 'located in spaces containing overlapping circular symbols indicating tree canopies, suggesting these facilities sit in unpaved, landscaped, or natural surface areas.' Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows no specific callouts or dimension lines indicating the distance from transformer pad locations to accessible parking/traffic areas. The plan shows landscaped areas around these eastern transformer locations but does not provide measurements demonstrating the 6-foot maximum distance to parking/traffic areas required by the grouping.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 and § 1.10.4 require that equipment pads (transformer pads) be within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck accessibility. The grouping specifies: 'Equipment pads: Within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck accessibility.' One transformer pad is clearly accessible (west side, adjacent to main driveway). However, the two transformer pads located on the east side of the property (near Buildings 4 and 6) are shown in landscaped areas with tree canopies. No dimension callouts verify that these locations are within 6 feet of drivable surfaces. The eastern transformer locations appear to be separated from the main parking/driveway circulation by buildings and landscaping. Without explicit dimension callouts or clear site plan notation showing 6-foot accessibility, compliance cannot be verified. This represents genuine ambiguity rather than clear non-compliance.
findings.comment: 24/7 truck access to transformer pad locations is not clearly shown or dimensioned on plans. Provide dimension callouts from each of the four transformer pad locations to the nearest accessible parking or traffic area, demonstrating that all transformers are within 6 feet of all-weather drivable surface suitable for bucket truck access per UCM § 1.10.4. If any transformer is more than 6 feet from accessible parking/traffic area, relocate or provide written approval from Austin Energy demonstrating acceptable maintenance access methodology.

applicableAreas: Below-grade distribution ductbank routes shown on electrical design plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric line routing denoted by solid blue lines labeled 'Underground Electric Line' connecting transformers, pull boxes, and building meters. Vision analysis confirms the presence of these facilities but notes: 'Access routes shown for electric facilities—There are NO explicitly labeled access routes (e.g., Electric Access Route or Maintenance Path) designated exclusively for electric facilities...pull boxes situated immediately adjacent to the main paved drive aisles and parking areas winding through the center of the complex, implying access via the general vehicular routes.' The plan shows ductbank routing via underground lines but provides no explicit verification that maintenance access along the entire length and width of the ductbank is available or unobstructed. No dimension callouts show clearance from proposed buildings or structures to ductbank routes. No profile or detail showing ductbank depth, burial, and protection is visible on the electrical plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires that access along the length and width of distribution ductbanks be maintained for Austin Energy maintenance trucks and equipment. The grouping specifies this deficiency occurs 'where below-grade distribution ductbanks exist or are proposed.' Sheet 21 shows ductbank routing, and vision analysis indicates pull boxes are accessible from main drive areas. However, the plan does not provide explicit verification that maintenance access is maintained along the entire ductbank length and width, or that no buildings, foundations, or permanent structures obstruct access. Without detailed ductbank profile sheets or maintenance access certification, compliance cannot be definitively confirmed. This is an area where the standard site plan information is insufficient, and supplementary details or clarification would be required.
findings.comment: Access along the length and width of below-grade distribution ductbanks is not explicitly shown or verified on plans. Provide a ductbank maintenance access plan (via utility plan cross-references or profile sheets) demonstrating that maintenance vehicles can access pull boxes and ductbank routes without obstruction from buildings, foundations, retaining walls, or permanent landscaping. Ensure all proposed structures maintain minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from ductbank routes per UCM § 1.10.5.
